description:
Once a pack write confirms, delete the constituents it subsumes.

This removes no data. The pack already holds every version its constituents did, so any subset that survives a crash is redundant rather than missing, and a rescan resolves it. No retention floor, policy input or coordination is involved — that is a separate, blocked ticket about reclaiming a pack whose contents exist nowhere else.

Order is write-then-delete and never the reverse. Deleting first would open a hole in the version range; the overlap left by the reverse order is already handled by the reader.

Wait a grace period between the confirmed put and the deletes, sized well above worst-case pull duration (the default pull timeout is 30s). That structurally precludes a reader which listed a key before the delete and fetches it after, rather than adding a guard for it. The residual, if a pull ever ran longer than the grace period, is a failed pull that gets retried — not lost data.

Delete order among constituents does not matter: the durable pack supersedes all of them.
title: Consolidator: delete constituents once their pack is durable
